stories.headline: Kate, Britain's Princess of Wales, to feature in documentary about cancer recovery
stories.summary: Kate, Britain's Princess of Wales, will reflect on her experience with cancer and recovery in a documentary to be broadcast internationally this month, Kensington Palace said on Saturday (21 November). The film, Heal, will premiere on the BBC on 29 November before airing in the United States, Australia and Canada.
stories.why_it_matters: Key fact to remember: Kate, Britain's Princess of Wales, will reflect on her experience with cancer and recovery in a documentary to be broadcast internationally this month, Kensington Palace said on Saturday (21 November). This is the one to carry into BCS/Bank questions on science and technology.
stories.exam_facts: The documentary will air on BBC One and BBC iPlayer in Britain on 29 November, before broadcasts on NBC in the United States, Channel 9 in Australia and CTV and Noovo in Canada. Kate, wife of heir-to-the-throne Prince William, announced in March 2024 that she was undergoing treatment for cancer after tests following major abdominal surgery found the disease. The documentary follows the princess as she completes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours in support of The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

stories.headline: Repeated cyclones, rain leave Dublar Char fishermen facing mounting losses during peak dried-fish season
stories.summary: According to Forest Department sources, this year's dried fish season began at Dublar Char on 30 October. Cyclone Arnab struck almost immediately, and with warning signal no 3 in force, the fishermen could not go to sea for the first five days of the season.

Dublar Char, on the Bay of Bengal shore next to the Sundarbans, produces 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes of dried fish a year, worth Tk300 crore to Tk350 crore or more, according to traders. An estimated 10,000 to 15,000 people work there as fishermen, fleet owners and labourers, locals said.

stories.summary: The central bank's Banking Regulation and Policy Department-2 renewed the request on 15 June 2026, but the ministry has yet to take action. stories.headline: Hefazat demands ban on Awami League as political party
stories.summary: In the statement, they said the Awami League had lost all political legitimacy in Bangladesh after allegedly being involved in enforced disappearances, killings and successive massacres during its 15 years in power. The organisation says the party has lost its political legitimacy over killings and mass atrocities during its 15 years in power, calling for a tribunal-led process to ban it.

The organisation said the political future of the party should not be decided without considering the wishes of the families of those killed and people injured in enforced disappearances, killings, the Pilkhana and Shapla incidents, and the July massacre under the previous Awami League government.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan weakens into low-pressure area, winter chill likely to increase from Tuesday
stories.summary: The impact of Cyclone Akvan on Bangladesh is beginning to ease, with rainfall expected to decrease from Tuesday (24 November) and mostly dry weather forecast across the country, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD). The outlook was detailed in the BMD's five-day forecast issued today (21 November) and signed by meteorologist Md Shahinul Islam.
